expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)
question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
rendered:
According to the document, after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS at 1C rates. 

The cathode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), which is an impressive mass specific performance especially with the moderate loading of 35 wt % active sulfur. 

The ratio of the two capacities implies that the sulfur content of the electrode is around 35/87 ≈ 0.40 or 40%. This is close to the 35 wt % active sulfur content stated in the paper.
